newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, then sinks on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, then sinks on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, then tumbled on ACCESS after the weekly AGA stock report showed an unexpectedly-small drawdown, sources said.

January gained 9.7 cents to close the day session at $3.493 per million British thermal units, then skidded to $3.36 on ACCESS. February settled 10.9 cents higher at $3.239. Other deferreds ended mixed.
"I think it was mostly technical today, but the AGAs were a lot lower than expected and the market reacted immediately," said one Texas-based trader, noting cash gained today.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 72 bcf to 75 percent of capacity, well-below expectations in the 84-92 bcf range. Stocks were still 214 bcf, or eight percent, below year-ago, but most expected the gap to narrow significantly in coming weeks, as declines fail to match last December's weekly average drawdown of 142 bcf.
With little extreme weather on the horizon but with stocks low and an uncertain winter still ahead, most saw little reason for prices to move far in either direction.
Technical traders pegged January support at $3.19, then $3.11 and then $3.04. Resistance was seen in the low-$3.50s and then at $3.70.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed 20 cents Wednesday to about the $3.40 level. Midcon pipes gained 15 cents or more to the mid-$3.30s. Gas at the New York City gate was talked little changed in the $4.05-4.10 range.
The 12-month strip gained 2.8 cents to $2.502. NYMEX said 43,305 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 36,450.

On the KCBT, January ended nine cents higher at $3.345, while deferreds closed up by one to to 10 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.7 cent to 14.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 233 lots traded, up from Tuesday's 168.
